dct_description_sm: The purpose of this project is to investigate how biotic interactions influence the movement of the tree line in Labrador.  As part of this project, my experiment will investigate the Stress Gradient Hypothesis (SGH).   The SGH was developed to explain the balance between interspecific competition and facilitation between young seedlings and their neighbours.  The hypothesis is centred on the idea of the Nurse Effect where seedlings growing in harsh environments have increased survival and growth rates when growing in association with a neighbouring Nurse Plant.  The aim of this study is to investigate aspects of the potential Nurse Effect between black spruce seedlings (Picea mariana) and a common shrub species in the region, Dwarf Birch (Betula glandulosa).
dct_title_s: Investigating the Nurse Effects of dwarf birch on black spruce seedlings during the first year of growth in the Mealy Mountains, Labrador
